answer: The proposed mechanisms by which GLP-1 receptor agonists reduce cardiovascular events are multifactorial and appear to extend beyond glycemic control, encompassing weight loss, blood pressure reduction, and lipid regulation [8]. Pleiotropic effects include anti-inflammatory actions, such as suppression of the NLRP3 inflammasome and promotion of an M2 macrophage phenotype, which contribute to more stable atherosclerotic plaques [10], as well as reductions in leptin and resistin and increases in anti-inflammatory adiponectin [6]. GLP-1 RAs also improve endothelial function via enhanced eNOS phosphorylation and nitric oxide production, reduce expression of adhesion molecules such as VCAM-1 and E-selectin, and inhibit ox-LDL-induced monocyte adhesion to endothelial cells [2][9][10]. Additional proposed mechanisms include anti-oxidative effects, blood pressure reduction through natriuresis and reduced sympathetic activity, and direct myocardial effects such as inhibition of cardiomyocyte apoptosis via the PKG/PKC/ERK pathway [8][9]. Mediation analyses indicate that 35%–55% of the cardiovascular benefit is independent of weight reduction [4]. However, it remains unclear exactly how these treatments contribute to their cardiovascular effects, and some argue that GLP-1 receptor expression in human myocardium and endothelial cells is too low to exert direct protective effects [7][8].
